Reading the spec and contracts skill before writing anything. Now reading the remaining supporting files before writing. Good. The foundry config already has `solc_version = "0.8.28"`, `evm_version = "cancun"`, optimizer 200 runs. Now writing all four files. Now writing the full test suite. This is large so split into two writes. Now running tests. Em dash in the string literal. Fixing that. Two test failures: `test_create_max_rate_boundary` (employer2 setup missing, should use existing employer) and `test_create_rate_above_max_reverts` (MAX_HOURLY_RATE + 1 = 1000e6+1 passes the rate check but escrow > MAX_ESCROW for long durations; need a valid duration for the test). Let me fix both. The `test_create_rate_above_max_reverts` issue is that `MAX_HOURLY_RATE + 1` is exactly `1_000_000_001` which is > `MAX_HOURLY_RATE`, so `hourlyRate > MAX_HOURLY_RATE` should revert with `InvalidAmount`. Let me check the contract condition again.

The contract has: `if (hourlyRate == 0 || hourlyRate > MAX_HOURLY_RATE) revert InvalidAmount();` — so `1_000e6 + 1` > `1_000e6` should revert. The test failure message was "next call did not revert as expected". This means the condition didn't fire. Let me check: `sp.MAX_HOURLY_RATE()` returns `1_000e6` = `1_000_000_000`. The `overRate` would be `1_000_000_001`. But the `employer` in `CreateShiftTest` already has unlimited approval and balance. So why didn't it revert?

Wait, looking again at the test failure output: `[FAIL: next call did not revert as expected] test_create_rate_above_max_reverts()`. This is the old version of the test which called `sp.createShift(worker, sp.MAX_HOURLY_RATE() + 1, DUR)`. `DUR = 3600`, so `escrow = (1_000e6 + 1) * 3600 / 3600 = 1_000e6 + 1`. That is > `MAX_HOURLY_RATE` (1_000e6), but `hourlyRate > MAX_HOURLY_RATE` where `hourlyRate = 1_000_000_001 > 1_000_000_000` -- this should revert.

Hmm, unless the test was using a local `employer2` that was set up wrong. But the old test used `vm.prank(employer)`. Let me look again...

Actually looking at the test: the old `test_create_rate_above_max_reverts` didn't have `vm.prank(employer)` in the original! No wait it did. Let me check the current file state to confirm the old code is gone and new code is there.

The new test uses `uint256 overRate = sp.MAX_HOURLY_RATE() + 1;` and `vm.prank(employer)`. This should work. Let me re-run.
